key_insight: Federated deep learning let two different cardiovascular cohorts improve risk prediction without sharing patient-level data.
clinical_relevance: This approach could support more privacy-preserving, cross-institution cardiovascular risk models that generalize better than single-site training.
method: Federated deep survival models trained across Lifelines and the Rotterdam Study
No central transfer of individual patient data
Performance compared with locally trained models
evidence_signal: On the Rotterdam Study, the C-statistic improved from 0.728 to 0.739, and on Lifelines from 0.783 to 0.787.
watch_item: The cohorts differed in size, population, and outcome definitions, so real-world deployment may need careful harmonization and validation.
paper_title: Federated Deep Learning for Privacy-Preserving Cardiovascular Disease Risk Prediction
